# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Attack Surface Reduction

Blocks the attack techniques from Defender's Attack Surface Reduction rules: macros that launch processes, executable content from email and USB, abuse of Office and script engines, and credential theft from LSASS.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog (endpointSecurityAttackSurfaceReduction) |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| Source | OpenIntuneBaseline Windows v4.0 — ES - Attack Surface Reduction - D - ASR Rules (L2) |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Attack_Surface_Reduction.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Attack_Surface_Reduction.json) |

> Replaces the previous ASR policy: the same 18 rules plus 2 new ones, all set to block.

## Standards

| Framework | Controls |
|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.8.7 Protection against malware<br>A.8.8 Management of technical vulnerabilities |
| NIS2 art. 21(2) | art. 21(2)(e) security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling |
| CIS Controls v8.1 | 10.5 Enable Anti-Exploitation Features |
| NIST CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-05<br>DE.CM-09 |

What this means per standard and what is needed organisationally alongside it: [COMPLIANCE.en.md](../../../docs/COMPLIANCE.en.md).
